author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Create and verify a personal PS2 disc image
summary: Dump an owned PS2 CD or DVD without altering it, preserve the correct track structure, verify the result, and recover cleanly from read errors before adding the image to EmuCoreX.
heroAlt: Media Preservation Frontend prepared to read a PlayStation 2 optical disc

blocks.text: Protect the disc and its structure

PlayStation 2 games ship on both CDs and DVDs. A DVD normally becomes a single ISO, while a CD can require a cue sheet plus one or more binary tracks so audio and data boundaries remain intact. Work only from a disc you own, clean the readable surface with straight centre-to-edge strokes, and use an optical drive that supports the media type. The objective is an exact preservation copy, not a compressed or patched image.
Never modify the master dump. Keep patches, translations and texture packs outside the original image so its hash remains a dependable recovery reference.

Use the current official PCSX2 disc guide for the operating system in front of you. On Windows, Media Preservation Frontend can drive Redumper and record drive details; the guide also documents ImgBurn. macOS and Linux have separate DVD and CD paths. Reserve enough free space for the image, logs and a second read, and disable sleep until the drive finishes.

items: The original personally owned PS2 disc and a compatible CD/DVD drive.
A destination on a healthy local SSD or HDD with at least twice the disc capacity free.
An official dumping tool for the current operating system.
A second empty output folder for verification.
No game, patcher or emulator actively reading the optical drive.

blocks.text: Read the disc without transforming it

items: 1. Identify whether the underside and label indicate CD or DVD, then select the matching workflow in the PCSX2 guide.
2. Scan the disc in MPF or select the optical drive manually; confirm PlayStation 2 media, the drive letter and an output folder you can recognize.
3. Start the dump and leave retry/error handling at the preservation tool's documented defaults. Do not eject, suspend Android/Windows, or browse the disc during the read.
4. Save every produced component and the tool log together. For CD media, keep the cue sheet beside its referenced binary tracks.
5. Repeat the read into a second folder. Compare byte sizes and SHA-256 hashes for every corresponding output file before importing the first verified set into EmuCoreX.

blocks.text: A green verification result in a supporting emulator is useful, but the strongest local check is two independent reads that produce identical files. Confirm that the game serial and region correspond to the physical label and that the image opens without write access. Launch a cold boot, reach a repeatable gameplay point, then exit normally before considering the dump ready for long-term storage.

items: Both reads have identical file counts, byte sizes and SHA-256 hashes.
A CD cue sheet references filenames that actually exist beside it.
The library detects the expected title and serial rather than an unrelated disc.
A cold boot reaches gameplay without a recurring read-error or loading freeze.
The private master is backed up separately and marked read-only.

blocks.text: When hashes disagree, preserve the logs and make a third read at a lower drive speed. Two matching results out of three identify the stable copy; repeated differences point to media damage or an unsuitable drive. If only a cue filename changed, repair the cue in a working copy and keep the untouched master. Do not fill unreadable sectors with data from an internet image.

items: Clean and inspect the disc, then retry with a slower speed.
Use another known-good optical drive when the same sector repeatedly fails.
Remove the unverified image from the library so it cannot accumulate saves around a faulty dump.
Restore the original cue/bin set from the private master if a conversion produced a broken working copy.
Freeze at the same loading point: often an unreadable or mismatched sector, not a graphics setting.
CD boots without music: cue sheet or audio tracks were discarded.
Emulator sees no game: archive was selected instead of an extracted supported image, or folder access was not granted.
Hashes change after patching: the master was modified; restore it and apply external patches instead.

blocks.text: Name the private folder with title, region, serial and dump date, but preserve original tool filenames inside it. A clean image plus its hashes and log is easier to audit than a library of vaguely named ISOs. When storage is tight, compress a backup with a lossless archival format only after verification and keep a playable working copy separate.
Follow the official PCSX2 disc-dumping guide
